rv.q: At 90 minutes it is a meal, not quite filling enough but every morsel delicious.
Eleanor Tindall’s meet cute queer love story is appropriately moving, but comes with a lot of very distracting baggage.

It’s a breathtaking dramatic experience, fuelled by an almost magical romance, unnerving tension, a creative team on song, and two leads who keep the Bush Theatre audience on tenderhooks almost the entire duration.

British reticence and awkwardness being what it is, it takes a while for the penny to drop, and even when it does, the narrative provides enough twists and turns to keep the audience guessing. Nadi Kemp-Sayfi (Ivy) (L) and Francesca Amewudah-Rivers (Ash) in 'Tender' at Bush Theatre.

cn.t: Critics praise this alluring dark romance for its phenomenal performances, particularly Francesca Amewudah-Rivers' taut and commanding presence, which anchors the intimate two-hander about tormented desire.
